Introduction to CALMeR

Sowmya Parthiban

Overview

CALMeR (Context-Aware Long-read MAPQ Rescuer) flags reads in long-read transcriptome BAM files whose MAPQ is anomalously low given their transcript context. It fits a Beta-Inflated (BEINF) regression model on a sampled subset of reads, computes randomized quantile residuals on the full table, and writes a filtered BAM plus a TSV of flagged reads.

The motivation: a uniform MAPQ threshold (e.g. samtools view -q 30) disproportionately discards reads from highly multi-isoform genes, GC-extreme transcripts, and long transcripts — not because the alignments are low quality but because these transcript-level properties systematically suppress MAPQ. CALMeR conditions on transcript context to distinguish noise from biology.

The standard pipeline is six steps; each function is one stage:

  1. extract_features() — read the BAM + GTF + transcriptome FASTA, build a per-read feature table (MAPQ, alignment length, transcript length, isoform count per gene, GC content, percent transcript covered).
  2. clean_features() — apply standard pre-fit filters (primary alignments only, n_isoforms cap, GC range, length range).
  3. fit_beinf() — fit a BEINF regression on a sampled subset.
  4. score_reads() — compute randomized quantile residuals for every read and flag those whose RQR falls in the lower tail.
  5. filter_bam() — write a filtered BAM (flagged reads removed) + a TSV of flagged reads with their feature values and residuals.
  6. calmer_report() — render an HTML or PDF diagnostic report.

End-to-end pipeline on bundled example data

CALMeR ships with a small example bundle (calmer_example_data()): ~2,000 reads from a real PCR cDNA long-read sample, a matching pruned GTF and transcriptome FASTA, plus a precomputed minimap2 self-alignment PAF.

library(CALMeR)
library(gamlss)   # so pb() resolves in user-supplied formulas

ex <- calmer_example_data()

# Compute the per-transcript paralog status table (cached PAF in the
# bundle; in production this would invoke minimap2 once per annotation).
paralog <- make_paralog_table(
    fasta    = ex$fasta,
    gtf      = ex$gtf,
    paf_path = ex$paf
)

features <- extract_features(ex$bam, ex$gtf, ex$fasta,
                             paralog_table = paralog)
clean    <- clean_features(features)

# pb() smoothers with a coarse 4-knot basis (inter = 4) on the four
# context predictors, plus a linear paralog term. The default pb() basis
# (inter = 20) is too flexible for the ~600-read bundled example and
# produces knot-driven wiggles in the partial-effects panels; a 4-knot
# basis keeps the smoother shape parameteric-like while still allowing
# mild non-linearity. On a real run with tens of thousands of reads,
# drop inter back to its default.
mu_rhs   <- y ~ pb(n_isoforms_sc,  inter = 4) + pb(tx_length_sc,   inter = 4) +
                pb(gc_content_sc,  inter = 4) + pb(pct_covered_sc, inter = 4) +
                max_pct_id_sc
nu_rhs   <-   ~ pb(n_isoforms_sc,  inter = 4) + pb(tx_length_sc,   inter = 4) +
                pb(gc_content_sc,  inter = 4) + pb(pct_covered_sc, inter = 4) +
                max_pct_id_sc

fit <- fit_beinf(
    clean, n = nrow(clean),
    predictors    = c("n_isoforms", "tx_length", "gc_content",
                      "pct_covered", "max_pct_id"),
    formula       = mu_rhs,
    sigma_formula = ~ 1,
    nu_formula    = nu_rhs,
    tau_formula   = nu_rhs
)

scored <- score_reads(features, fit, filter_method = "mad",
                      threshold = -3)
#> score_reads: 14 reads have n_isoforms outside training range [1, 10]; marking unscored.
#> score_reads: 5 reads have tx_length outside training range [200, 7967]; marking unscored.

Filtered outputs

filter_bam() writes a filtered BAM (flagged reads removed) and a gzipped TSV listing the flagged reads with their feature values and residuals. Internal scaled-predictor columns (*_sc) are dropped from the TSV — the file keeps the columns a user would actually inspect.

filt <- filter_bam(
    bam     = ex$bam,
    scored  = scored,
    out_bam = tempfile(fileext = ".bam"),
    out_tsv = tempfile(fileext = ".tsv.gz")
)
#> filter_bam: 628 alignments in, 2 flagged reads (2 alignments removed), 626 alignments kept.

Diagnostic report (rendered inline)

The chunk below pulls in inst/rmd/diagnostic_report.Rmd as a child document and renders it inline as part of this vignette. All sections of the standalone report — predictor definitions, training summary, model fit, model comparison, residual diagnostics, partial effects, scoring summary, where flags landed — appear below.

Predictors

CALMeR conditions MAPQ on the following per-read / per-transcript features. Default clean_features() filters are listed alongside; ranges shown in the partial-effects plots may be tighter (e.g. n_isoforms is capped at 7 in the partial-effect panel for visual clarity).

Predictor What it measures How it’s computed Default clean_features() filter
n_isoforms Number of annotated isoforms of the gene that the read’s target transcript belongs to. n_distinct(transcript_id) per gene_id, from the GTF. <= 10
tx_length Length of the target transcript in nucleotides. Sum of exon widths per transcript_id, from the GTF. [100, 10000] bp
gc_content GC composition of the target transcript. (G + C) / length from the transcriptome FASTA. [30, 70]%
pct_covered Fraction of the target transcript spanned by the read alignment. min(alignment_length / tx_length, 1), from the BAM CIGAR + GTF. none (uses full 0-100% range)
max_pct_id (if present) Highest cross-gene transcript-level identity for the target. Captures paralog ambiguity. minimap2 self-alignment of the transcriptome FASTA, then max(pct_id) over hits with alen >= 50 and query_cov >= 70%, restricted to cross-gene pairs. none (raw 0-100%; 0 = no paralog)

The partial-effects plot caps n_isoforms at 7 for the x-axis even when training data extends higher, since most of the predictive content sits in the 1-7 range and very high values become sparse.

2. Model fit

Formulas used:

  • \(\mu\): y ~ pb(n_isoforms_sc, inter = 4) + pb(tx_length_sc, inter = 4) + pb(gc_content_sc, inter = 4) + pb(pct_covered_sc, inter = 4) + max_pct_id_sc
  • \(\sigma\): ~1
  • \(\nu\): ~pb(n_isoforms_sc, inter = 4) + pb(tx_length_sc, inter = 4) + pb(gc_content_sc, inter = 4) + pb(pct_covered_sc, inter = 4) + max_pct_id_sc
  • \(\tau\): ~pb(n_isoforms_sc, inter = 4) + pb(tx_length_sc, inter = 4) + pb(gc_content_sc, inter = 4) + pb(pct_covered_sc, inter = 4) + max_pct_id_sc

2b. Model comparison

Refits on the same training data with two alternative parameterizations: (i) linear terms in \(\mu\), \(\nu\), \(\tau\) (this is what the user supplied if no spline override was given), and (ii) penalized B-splines with five interior knots in all three. \(\sigma\) is held to an intercept-only formula in both, since modeling the beta-interior precision usually doesn’t help on data of this size. AIC, BIC, and gamlss’s pseudo-\(R^2\) are reported alongside the user-supplied fit.

Model fit metrics on the training data. Lower AIC/BIC and higher pseudo-\(R^2\) are better.

4. Partial effects on E[MAPQ]

Each panel varies one predictor over its training range while holding the others at their training median, and shows the model’s expected MAPQ:

\[ E[Y] \;=\; \frac{\tau + \mu}{1 + \nu + \tau}, \qquad E[\mathrm{MAPQ}] = 60 \cdot E[Y] \]

Partial effects on E[MAPQ].
